common_conf: This is an optional configuration file read by \fBgpg\fP on
startup.  It may contain options pertaining to all components of
GnuPG.  Its current main use is for the "use-keyboxd" option.  If
the default home directory \(oq\fI~/.gnupg\fP\(cq does not exist, GnuPG creates
this directory and a \(oq\fIcommon.conf\fP\(cq file with "use-keyboxd".
cross: When verifying a signature made from a subkey, ensure that the cross
certification "back signature" on the subkey is present and valid.  This
protects against a subtle attack against subkeys that can sign.
dearmor: Pack or unpack an arbitrary input into/from an OpenPGP ASCII armor.
This is a GnuPG extension to OpenPGP and in general not very useful.
The \fB\-\-dearmor\fP command can also be used to dearmor PEM armors.

keyring: .B  \-\-keyring \fIfile\fP
Add \fIfile\fP to the current list of keyrings. If \fIfile\fP begins
with a tilde and a slash, these are replaced by the $HOME directory. If
the filename does not contain a slash, it is assumed to be in the GnuPG
home directory ("~/.gnupg" unless \fB\-\-homedir\fP or $GNUPGHOME is
used).
Note that this adds a keyring to the current list. If the intent is to
use the specified keyring alone, use \fB\-\-keyring\fP along with
\fB\-\-no\-default\-keyring\fP.
If the option \fB\-\-no\-keyring\fP has been used no keyrings will
be used at all.
Note that if the option \fBuse\-keyboxd\fP is enabled in
\(oq\fIcommon.conf\fP\(cq, no keyrings are used at all and keys are all
maintained by the keyboxd process in its own database.
lock_never: Disable locking entirely. This option should be used only in very
special environments, where it can be assured that only one process
is accessing those files. A bootable floppy with a stand-alone
encryption system will probably use this. Improper usage of this
option may lead to data and key corruption.

no_autostart: Do not start the gpg-agent or the dirmngr if it has not yet been
started and its service is required.  This option is mostly useful on
machines where the connection to gpg-agent has been redirected to
another machines.  If dirmngr is required on the remote machine, it
may be started manually using \fBgpgconf \-\-launch dirmngr\fP.

option and do not provide alternate keyrings via \fB\-\-keyring\fP,
then GnuPG will still use the default keyring.

no_options: Shortcut for \fB\-\-options /dev/null\fP. This option is detected
before an attempt to open an option file.  Using this option will also
prevent the creation of a \(oq\fI~/.gnupg\fP\(cq homedir.
no_sig_cache: Do not cache the verification status of key signatures.
Caching gives a much better performance in key listings. However, if
you suspect that your public keyring is not safe against write
modifications, you can use this option to disable the caching. It
probably does not make sense to disable it because all kind of damage
can be done if someone else has write access to your public keyring.
no_use_agent: This is dummy option. \fBgpg\fP always requires the agent.
pubring_kbx: The public keyring using the new keybox format.  This file is shared
with \fBgpgsm\fP.  You should backup this file.  See above for
the relation between this file and it predecessor.

verify: Assume that the first argument is a signed file and verify it without
generating any output.  With no arguments, the signature packet is
read from STDIN.  If only one argument is given, the specified file is
expected to include a complete signature.
With more than one argument, the first argument should specify a file
with a detached signature and the remaining files should contain the
signed data. To read the signed data from STDIN, use \(oq\-\(cq as the
second filename.  For security reasons, a detached signature will not
read the signed material from STDIN if not explicitly specified.

This program is actually a stripped-down version of \fBgpg\fP which is
only able to check signatures. It is somewhat smaller than the fully-blown
\fBgpg\fP and uses a different (and simpler) way to check that
the public keys used to make the signature are valid. There are
no configuration files and only a few options are implemented.
